LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 2.3.1 SUBJECT-VERB AGREEMENT

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: Language use 2.3.1 Subject-verb agreement
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language use 2.3.1 Subject-verb agreement, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: How do you talk about person, an object or a place? 2. How do we talk about many people?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language use 2.3.1 Subject-verb agreement together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration: The learner articulates signs or fingerspell effectively as they recite poems featuring singular and plural forms.

Learning to learn: The learner learns independently as they individually construct sentences about actions demonstrated by peers.

Values:
Responsibility: self-drive is promoted as learners take roles in pair and group activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: self-esteem is nurtured as the learner constructs simple sentences with correct subject-verb agreement.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learners relate grammatical items (subject-verb agreement) to sentence construction learnt in Kenyan Sign Language, Kiswahili Language
